# Introduction 

This document is the user guide of the REST API for Product Usage Catalog Management. It includes the data model definition as well as all available operations for the ProductUsageSpecification resource.

The Product Usage Catalog Management API provides a standardized mechanism for Product Usage Catalog management such as the creation, update, retrieval of a collection of Product Usage Specification. A Product Usage Specification defines how usage details are collected for a Product that is charged or metered for usage (for example a mobile voice product). A Product Usage Specification is a catalog representation of a usage of a Product; it defines the characteristics of the usage associated with a Product Specification.

The Product Usage Catalog API manages the ProductUsageSpecification resource:

- A ProductUsageSpecification represents a catalog view of the targeted ProductUsage, comprised of characteristics specifications which define all the attributes known for that particular type of usage.
- The main attributes are its id, lastUpdate, related ProductUsageSpecification, characteristics specifications, lifecycleStatus
- A ProductUsageSpecification follows a simple lifecycle which is presented below.

The Product Usage Catalog API performs the following operations on the ProductUsageSpecification resource:

- Creation of a ProductUsageSpecification
- Retrieval of a ProductUsageSpecification or a collection of ProductUsageSpecification, depending on filter criteria
- Partial update of a ProductUsageSpecification
- Deletion of a ProductUsageSpecification

Note : TMF635 Product Usage Management API manages ProductUsage events that represents the structured report of a service that has been delivered, guided to a product, and is considered billable. Each ProductUsage event is defined by a corresponding ProductUsageSpecification, which standardizes what type of usage occurred (e.g., voice, data session, API call) and its associated characteristics (e.g., duration, data consumption, correlation identifier). TMF767 Product Usage Catalog Management API is responsible for managing ProductUsageSpecifications that represents a catalog view of the targeted ProductUsage comprised of characteristics specifications which define all the attributes know for the particular usage

| inTest | When the design is approved |
| active | When the test is OK then its status is changed to“active”. When a ProductUsageSpecification is ina “active” status it means, it has been validatedand tested, and can be referred by aProductSpecification available for customers. |
| obsolete | When no more customer holds any Product beingan instantiation of a ProductSpecification referringto this ProductUsageSpecification, its status ischanged to “obsolete” meaning it can be removedfrom the catalog. |

### Information Framework excerpts:

Put simply, usage is how much service is used, by whom is it used, where and when is it used and circumstances under which it is used.

The UsageSpecification class describes a type of usage. In order to achieve a flexible structure of the UsageSpecification all its attributes are stored as characteristics.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The Usage class represents a usage event. It is described by the UsageSpecification and comprised of UsageCharacteristicValues that hold data attributes of a usage specified by UsageSpecCharacteristics. The UsageCharacteristic can either store its value in the usageCharValue property or reference predefined UsageSpecCharacteristicValue.

The ProductUsageSpec is defined for the certain ProductSpecification.

Note that the API representation of Information Framework model is partial. In particular the direct relationship between a ProductUsage (that would be originated from a ResourceUsage) and a ResourceUsage is not implemented because of lack of business need for this.

Note that Information Framework and API specification may evolve independently but tend to be consistent as much as possible.

## Sample Use Cases 

### Use Cases

Main use cases for the Product Usage Catalog API are :

- The creation of a product usage specification as part of product development of a new service
- The management of existing product usage specifications as part of changes to services refected in the product level
- The association of product usage specifications in the definition of product specifications
- Retrieval of the product usage specifications to be able to understand the characteristics of the product usages

The TMFS012 Product Catalog – Launching a New Product Offering should cover the use of this API. In its existing version it doesn’t yet, that’s why there are no excerpts of this use case in this document yet. The reader can still have a look on it as the document will evolve to cover this API. ([https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs012-use-](https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs012-use-case-product-catalog-launching-a-new-product-offering-v2-0-2/) [case-product-catalog-launching-a-new-product-offering-v2-0-2/)](https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs012-use-case-product-catalog-launching-a-new-product-offering-v2-0-2/)

Currently the examples in this User Guide and OAS file come from the TMFS005 Use Case Billing Fiber Contract ([https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs005-](https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs005-billing-fiber-contract-v2-2-0/) [billing-fiber-contract-v2-2-0/)](https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs005-billing-fiber-contract-v2-2-0/) and TMFS009 Use Case Usage and Balance Management ([https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs009-use-case-usage-and-](https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs009-use-case-usage-and-balance-management-v6-1-0/) [balance-management-v6-1-0/)](https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfs009-use-case-usage-and-balance-management-v6-1-0/) documents.

Note that these two url will propose latest version of the documents.

Note that TMFS005 and TMFS009 show the data model but it doesn’t really provide the use case for this API. Those two documents are both more related to the creation of the actual ProductUsage in the inventory and where the ProductUsageSpecification plays the role of explaining the characteristics used for the given service.

- Creation of a simple ProductUsageSpecification for International Voice of a Fix Communication ProductSpecification. This ProductUsageSpecification is defined by some characteristics of a Fix Communication voice call (originating phone number, destination phone number, start and stop date-and-time…); listing ProductUsageSpecification’s at version 2.5; retrieving a single ProductUsageSpecification based on its id; updating the ProductUsageSpecification for a simple change; and ultimately its deletion based on the same id.

Note that entities and characteristic names don’t always fully match but the meaning should match.

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a StringCharacteristic and BooleanCharacteristic inheriting properties from the abstract Characteristic entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Characteristic instances some may be instances of StringCharacteristic where other could be instances of BooleanCharacteristic. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of the Product Usage API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance a ProductUsageSpecificationRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as ProductUsageSpecificationRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

## RESOURCE MODEL 

### Managed Entity and Task Resource Models

### ProductUsageSpecification resource

A detailed description of a product usage specification that are of interest to the business and can have product offering prices applied to it. It is comprised of characteristic specification, which define all attributes and their possible values known for a particular type of product usage.

A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

### Updates partially a ProductUsageSpecification `PATCH /productUsageSpecification/{id}?fields=…`

**Description** This operation allows partial updates of a ProductUsageSpecification entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| lastUpdate |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| attachment |  |
| description |  |
| lifecycleStatus |  |
| name |  |
| productSpecification |  |
| serviceUsageSpecification |  |
| specCharacteristic |  |
| targetProductUsageSchema |  |
| validFor |  |
| version |  |

# API NOTIFICATIONS 

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

# Acknowledgements 

## Release Notes

### v5.0.0

- TMF767 first stable version
- productUsageSpecification is an evolution of usageSpecification from TMF635 Usage Management API v4.0.0 which name change from usageSpecification to productUsageSpecification

**schemas changes**

- productUsageSpecification : entitySpecRelationship removed (the link with the other specifications are specific attributes)
- productUsageSpecification : productSpecification added to give the reference to the ProductSpecification that to which the ProductUsageSpecification(s) is attached
- productUsageSpecification : serviceUsageSpecification added to give reference to serviceUsageSpecification(s) involved for the creation of this product usage specification.
- productUsageSpecification : relatedParty removed as no general need for it
- productUsageSpecification : constraint removed as no API exposes Constraint entity
- productUsageSpecification : targetEntitySchema replaced by targetProductUsageSchema
- productUsageSpecification : name and lifecycleStatus are required attribute for the creation operation
